strategies.overview: With a high Attack stat and access to Sharpness and Stone Axe, Kleavor is very consistent in dishing out great damage while setting up Stealth Rock. Moreover, with access to STAB U-turn, Kleavor can opt to run Choice Scarf sets, as it outspeeds common Choice Scarf Pokemon such as Basculegion-F and Gardevoir. Kleavor is a great lead for offensive teams, as its main utility in Stone Axe gives it an advantage over other Stealth Rock leads such as Terrakion and Azelf, which Taunt cripples. Kleavor also has Swords Dance, which allows it to not be as passive and one-dimensional as the other leads. U-turn also allows Kleavor to pivot out of defensive switch-ins such as Hippowdon, Jirachi, and Registeel and gain momentum for the team. However, Kleavor is rather frail defensively, and being weak to Stealth Rock hinders its ability to work as a momentum generator. Ultimately, as a lead, Kleavor has a low Speed stat compared to other leads, which makes it being prone to Iron Head from Jirachi and Rock Blast from Terrakion.
strategies.comments:
Other Options

Heavy-Duty Boots + Swords Dance is a good option for pivot Kleavor, as it mitigates the Stealth Rock weakness and makes Kleavor more offensively threatening. Tailwind is an option on lead sets, as Kleavor can set it up before fainting to threaten foes offensively, allowing naturally slow Pokemon such as Armarouge and Feraligatr be more threatening. Covert Cloak is also an option to avoid getting flinched by Iron Head Jirachi, as it is a main form of counterplay versus lead Kleavor hyper offense teams. One could also opt to run Choice Band, which works similar to Choice Scarf, but losing the ability to outspeed Choice Scarf Gardevoir, Basculegion-F, and common faster Pokemon such as Krookodile and Jirachi is unappealing. Tera Bug X-Scissor has a good chance to OHKO Amoonguss and Slowbro and can 2HKO Chesnaught.

Checks and Counters

Anti-leads: Jirachi outspeeds Kleavor and threatens to KO or flinch it with Iron Head. Rock Blast Terrakion naturally outspeeds Kleavor and needs three hits to KO Kleavor, and it is a popular anti-Kleavor lead. If Kleavor cannot set up Stealth Rock, it gives the opposing team a huge advantage, as Stealth Rock allows hyper offense teams to break through opposing teams much more easily.

Faster Choice Scarf Users: Faster Choice Scarf users such as Krookodile and Jirachi outspeed and threaten to KO Choice Scarf Kleavor after some chip damage.

Physically Defensive Pokemon: Defensive Pokemon such as Hippowdon, Chesnaught, and Amoonguss shrug off hits from non-Swords Dance Kleavor sets and threaten it back with STAB moves such as Earthquake from Hippowdon, Body Press from Chesnaught, and Foul Play from Amoonguss.

Entry Hazards: Kleavor is weak to Stealth Rock, rendering Choice Scarf sets crippled and unable to pivot as effectively once Stealth Rock is active.

Steel-types: Kleavor is checked by Steel-types such as Registeel and Hisuian Goodra if it is not using Close Combat or is locked into Stone Axe. Bisharp also can set up on non-Close Combat Kleavor and threaten to sweep the team. Bisharp in particular is very threatening against hyper offense teams, as it has a great matchup against the archetype.

movesets.name: Lead
movesets.description:
Set Details

Swords Dance threatens defensive leads such as Hippowdon and Gastrodon, and STAB X-Scissor will threaten to 2HKO them. This usually ends up with Hippowdon or Gastrodon weakened, which makes it easier for Kleavor's teammates to KO them. Close Combat allows Kleavor to hit Steel-types such as Hisuian Goodra, Empoleon, and Registeel. Trailblaze boosts Kleavor's Speed and makes it a threatening sweeper, and it is especially good against offensive teams, as they do not have a solid defensive backbone and often rely on outspeeding and KOing Kleavor. Focus Sash prevents Kleavor from being KOed by faster Choice Scarf Pokemon such as Basculegion-F and Stone Edge Terrakion. Tera Ghost is used to block Rapid Spin from Cyclizar, though Kleavor should rarely Terastallize due to the value Terastallization brings to its teammates.

This is the standard lead Kleavor set on a hyper offense team. Common hyper offense teammates such as Terrakion, Bisharp, and Mimikyu appreciate Kleavor's ability to set up Stealth Rock reliably. These Pokemon will have an easier time sweeping due to Kleavor setting up Stealth Rock and weakening physical walls such as Hippowdon. Other hyper offense staples that are weak to Stealth Rock such as Weakness Policy Armarouge can struggle on teams with lead Kleavor, since Kleavor cannot prevent other leads such as Terrakion and Azelf from setting up Stealth Rock, making Maushold a great teammate due to having entry hazard control in Tidy Up, as well as being a strong setup sweeper.

movesets.name: Choice Scarf
movesets.description:
Set Details

Choice Scarf Kleavor takes advantage of U-turn and its decent base Speed to be a hard-hitting pivot while also being able to set up entry hazards. Choice Scarf allows Kleavor to outspeed common Choice Scarf Pokemon such as Gardevoir and Basculegion-F. Other Choice Scarf users able to set up hazards do exist in RU, mainly Krookodile, but it has to decide whether to set up Stealth Rock or attack; Kleavor bypasses that due to having access to Stone Axe. U-turn allows Kleavor to pivot out of bad matchups such as Hippowdon and Chesnaught and gives the team momentum. Close Combat hits Steel-types such as Hisuian Goodra, Empoleon, and Registeel. Tera Fighting flips Kleavor's Stealth Rock weakness and lets Close Combat OHKO Empoleon, Krookodile, and Hisuian Goodra.

Choice Scarf Kleavor fits on bulky offense teams and acts as one of the main momentum generators of the team. As a result, Pokemon that can take advantage of safe switch-ins are preferred teammates, such as Basculegion-F and Armarouge. Kleavor usually wants to use U-turn as the foe switches into Steel-type teammates such as Jirachi, Registeel, and Hisuian Goodra, and these teammates take advantage of the safe switch in as well as threaten them offensively. VoltTurn cores with Mienshao and Magnezone can take advantage of the aforementioned Steel-types as well as Chesnaught and Talonflame that tend to switch into Kleavor. Having access to entry hazard control is almost mandatory for Kleavor, as its weakness to Stealth Rock cripples its effectiveness. As a result, Pokemon such as Cyclizar, Noivern, and Talonflame are good partners. Pokemon such as Slowbro, Hippowdon, and Palossand that can deal with faster Choice Scarf users such as Jirachi and Mienshao are appreciated.

movesets.name: Choice Scarf (Bug)
movesets.description:
Equipped with a Choice Scarf, Kleavor can leverage its naturally high Attack stat, Sharpness ability, and Stone Axe to pressure the opposing team, notably outspeeding Dragapult, Flutter Mane, and Ogerpon-H. Stone Axe smashes through Fire- and Flying-types such as Volcarona, Ogerpon-H, and Zapdos. Night Slash deals with offensive Ghost foes like Dragapult, Spectrier, and Gholdengo. Alternatively, X-Scissor destroys Dark threats like Meowscarada, Greninja, and Darkrai, avoiding hit-and-run with U-turn. Close Combat helps deal with Steel foes such as Bisharp, Heatran, and Iron Treads that would otherwise pose trouble.

Given its frailty and weakness to Rock-type moves, Forretress is a valuable partner for Kleavor, spinning away entry hazards and setting its own, taking advantage of Stone Axe to run Spikes; they also form a potent VoltTurn core thanks to Forretress's access to Volt Switch to slow pivot into Kleavor. Araquanid is another beneficial teammate, (AC) as it can set Sticky Web to ensure Kleavor outspeeds the whole metagame, even Choice Scarf variants of fast Pokemon like Dragapult and Flutter Mane, and Ceruledge after Weak Armor. Additionally, Araquanid can sponge Water-type moves from Swampert and Keldeo and weaken them enough for Kleavor to finish them. Offensively, Lokix and Scizor are both very solid teammates that can dent the opposing team for Kleavor and appreciate the utility provided by Stone Axe. More specifically, Lokix is best at dealing with Ghost-types like Gholdengo and Sinistcha and offers strong priority options with Sucker Punch and First Impression to pick up KOs in Psychic, Ghost, and Dark matchups. Scizor shines in Fairy and Rock matchups with its Technician-boosted Bullet Punch and Swords Dance, taking advantage of the chip damage provided by Stone Axe to avoid being stopped by Focus Sash. Volcarona is another premier partner, capable of addressing the Fighting matchup by disposing of Urshifu-R and Great Tusk with Psychic and by burning Iron Hands with Flame Body or Will-O-Wisp.

movesets.name: Choice Scarf (Rock)
movesets.description:
Kleavor finds a solid place on Rock-type teams thanks to a unique secondary Bug typing, granting it neutrality to Fighting- and Grass- type attacks. Stone Axe is a consistently strong attack, deleting Fire-types like Ogerpon-H and Ceruledge and neutral targets like Flutter Mane. It also sets up Stealth Rock unconditionally, clearing up moveslots for the rest of the team. Close Combat serves a crucial role in allowing Kleavor to hit Steel-types like Heatran and Hisuian Goodra that would otherwise wall it. Night Slash provides utility in allowing Kleavor to hit Gholdengo, which otherwise also walls it, along with being able to hit other Ghost-types like Dragapult and Spectrier. Meanwhile, X-Scissor provides a strong secondary STAB move that can remove Bug-weak targets like Ogerpon-W, Hoopa-U, and Slowbro reliably. U-turn provides a solid pivot tool along with a Bug-type attack should Kleavor forgo X-Scissor.

Ogerpon-C serves as an invaluable teammate, being able to threaten the Water-types that easily scare Kleavor out such as Toxapex, Swampert, and Keldeo. Glimmora provides incredible utility with Mortal Spin, which removes entry hazards, as well as its ability Toxic Debris, which helps to wear down threats that are weak to Toxic Spikes such as Iron Hands, the Ogerpon formes, and Great Tusk. Glimmora can also opt for Choice Specs, allowing it to remove physical walls like Toxapex, Corviknight, and Skarmory with minimal issue. Choice Band Hisuian Arcanine can remove Steel-types that can wall Kleavor such as Skarmory, Corviknight, and Gholdengo while also appreciating Kleavor's Stealth Rock chipping other threats down into OHKO range for Hisuian Arcanine's Rock-type STAB move such as Toxapex. Alternatively, Hisuian Arcanine can run a set with Substitute more reliably deal with threats like Kingambit, which prove problematic for Kleavor. Choice Band Iron Boulder, with its Psychic typing, can remove bulky Fighting- and Poison-types like Iron Hands, Okidogi, and Pecharunt that can otherwise easily set up on Kleavor. Iron Boulder can also serve as a devastating second Choice Scarf user, being able to outspeed threats like Meowscarada and Greninja and easily remove them. Tyranitar provides sand support, chipping targets down along with Thunder Wave to slow down opposing Choice Scarf threats such as Latias and Flutter Mane. Rhyperior, thanks to its immense physical bulk, can come in and remove troublesome targets like Gliscor, Iron Treads, and Sneasler. Setup sweepers such as Minior and Drednaw both appreciate Kleavor setting up Stealth Rock, making targets that may have been able to take hits, such as Toxapex, Great Tusk, and Arcahludon, fall.

movesets.name: Timber!
movesets.description:
• While Stone Axe's accuracy can be off-putting if reliable Stealth Rock setting is a must, Kleavor's unique form of role compression makes it an effective alternative to more defensive setters.

  • Night Slash: Night Slash is Kleavor's best way of dealing big damage to Gholdengo and is a reliable option against weakened Flutter Mane.

  • Feint: Feint's increased priority over other priority attacks make it a great way to pick off Focus Sash foes like Chien-Pao and Iron Bundle. Kleavor being faster means it'll even outpace Dragonite's Extreme Speed!

  • Trailblaze: While Kleavor isn't known for easily sweeping, it's fast enough to outspeed Flutter Mane and Iron Bundle after Trailblaze, and Trailblaze is especially useful when using Tera Grass against Urshifu-R.

  • X-Scissor versus Close Combat: While X-Scissor's coverage on paper isn't impressive, the boost from Sharpness lets it 2HKO Cresselia and Ting-Lu that lack Sitrus Berry.

  • Adamant versus Jolly: If using Feint, Adamant is the best nature choice for maximizing the amount of targets it can pick off after using Stone Axe. For Trailblaze variants, Jolly is preferred to outspeed Flutter Mane, Iron Bundle, and even Dragapult. Jolly also ensures it outspeeds all Gholdengo that lack Choice Scarf.

Other Options
  • Tailwind: Tailwind is an unusual move for Battle Stadium Singles, but Kleavor's disposable nature with Focus Sash can make it justified as a move to use before fainting.
Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Kleavor's entry hazard setting nature may not make Terastallization seem important, but its archnemesis, Urshifu-R, makes it worth considering, since it can threaten to OHKO Kleavor through its Focus Sash.

  • Grass: Tera Grass is a good response against Urshifu-R, not only resisting its deadly Surging Strikes, but also boosting Trailblaze.

  • Water: Tera Water isn't as offensively useful, but it's still a good way to resist both Surging Strikes and powerful Steel-type attacks like Heatran's Flash Cannon.

  • Bug: Tera Bug isn't great defensively, but it allows Kleavor to 2HKO even Impish Sitrus Berry Ting-Lu with X-Scissor.

  • Ghost: Despite Kleavor's resistance to Extreme Speed, Dragonite often picks off Focus Sash variants, so Tera Ghost is a huge shock for it, though a rather risky Terastallization choice. It also blocks Rapid Spin from Great Tusk, even if it's not particularly common.

Items

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash makes Kleavor a good lead against a wide variety of foes such as Iron Bundle and lets it easily justify the maximum Speed investment needed to outspeed Gholdengo.

  • Assault Vest: Kleavor's special bulk is mediocre at best, but Stone Axe's entry hazard setting powers can justify using Assault Vest to survive certain attacks that are otherwise impossible without Focus Sash.

Assault Vest EV Spreads

  • 28 HP / 204 Atk / 4 Def / 204 SpD / 68 Spe with Adamant: This more specially bulky spread usually survives Iron Bundle's Hydro Pump, Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Tera Fairy Moonblast, and Jolly Life Orb Chien-Pao's Icicle Crash while outspeeding Garchomp after one use of Trailblaze.

  • 28 HP / 108 Atk / 4 Def / 204 SpD / 164 Spe with Jolly: This spread has enough Speed to outspeed Iron Bundle after using Trailblaze once while usually surviving Timid Tera Fairy Choice Specs Moonblast from Flutter Mane, Non-Choice Specs Iron Bundle's Hydro Pump, and Jolly Life Orb Chien-Pao's Icicle Crash.

  • 140 HP / 52 Atk / 4 Def / 244 SpD / 68 Spe with Adamant: This more extreme spread usually lets Kleavor survive even Timid Gholdengo's Make It Rain, almost always avoids a 2HKO from Modest Chi-Yu's Dark Pulse, and avoids an OHKO from Adamant Life Orb Chien-Pao's Icicle Crash while still outspeeding Garchomp after one use of Trailblaze.

Minor Optimizations
  • Female Gender: While very rare, Cute Charm Enamorus can potentially impact Kleavor, meaning there are no drawbacks to using a female gender.

movesets.name: Choice Scarf
movesets.description:
• Choice Scarf Kleavor has a very unique niche of being a decent revenge killing pivot that can set up Stealth Rock at the same time!

  • Night Slash: Night Slash is Kleavor's best move against Gholdengo, making it highly recommended, since Kleavor outspeeds it.

  • X-Scissor versus Close Combat: Despite offering less coverage, X-Scissor's sheer power with Sharpness makes it a great option, dealing heavy damage to Cresselia and Ting-Lu and being a strong cleaning option. Close Combat isn't as reliable, but it can let Kleavor more reliably revenge kill threats such as Tera Normal Dragonite and Ursaluna. It's also Kleavor's easiest option to use for revenge killing Urshifu-R.

Other Options
  • Aerial Ace: Aerial Ace isn't particularly strong despite the boost from Sharpness, but it does deal massive damage to Urshifu-R, especially if using the easily accessible Tera Flying.
Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: While Choice Scarf Urshifu-R is still a major concern, this set's other purpose means that setting up Stealth Rock is required for success, making Terastallization less important.

  • Bug: If using X-Scissor, Tera Bug lets Kleavor 2HKO even Sitrus Berry Ting-Lu, making for an effective late-game cleaner.

  • Grass: If Choice Scarf Urshifu-R is a major concern, Tera Grass is a decent way around it in addition to getting an advantage against Breloom leads.

  • Flying: Tera Flying should only be used with Aerial Ace, which gives Kleavor a 75% chance of OHKOing Urshifu-R after taking Stealth Rock damage.

Minor Optimizations
  • Female Gender: Cute Charm Enamorus is very rare and not important, but it does mean that a female gender is slightly preferred on Kleavor.

strategies.overview:
Draft Order: Round 6 onwards

Price Range: 5-6 points

Overview: Kleavor serves as a utility Pokemon, as its unique ability to set up Stealth Rock while also dealing damage makes it a valuable asset. In addition, access to both U-turn and Defog furthers its role as a utility pivot. Kleavor can hit hard with its combination of high Attack and Sharpness-boosted STAB moves; however, its Speed and bulk are mediocre, it has a very unideal typing both offensively and defensively, and its movepool is shallow, thus necessitating the right conditions to allow it to properly function.
strategies.comments:
Common Roles

Suicide Lead: Stone Axe allows Kleavor to reliably deal lots of damage to foes while setting Stealth Rock. However, due to its mediocre Speed and bulk, it often requires either a Focus Sash or Choice Scarf to ensure it is able to get a Stone Axe off.

Wallbreaker: Kleavor's high Attack combined with Sharpness makes it an effective wallbreaker. Its damage can be further boosted by Swords Dance or Choice Band, but it often wants to run Heavy-Duty Boots when it is expected to pivot frequently.

Revenge Killer: A Choice Scarf allows Kleavor to overcome its lackluster Speed and revenge kill foes with its powerful Sharpness-boosted Stone Axe and X-Scissor. In addition, access to a fast U-turn allows it to maintain momentum.

Common Moves

Primary STAB Moves: Stone Axe, Rock Blast, U-turn, X-Scissor

Setup Moves: Swords Dance, Trailblaze, Agility

Utility Moves: Defog, Substitute, Brick Break, Roar

Coverage: Close Combat, Night Slash, Aerial Ace, Slash

Niche Moves

Pounce / Rock Tomb: Pounce and Rock Tomb allow Kleavor to hinder foes by lowering their Speed, potentially allowing it or any of its allies to be faster the next turn.

Reversal: When Reversal is used alongside Endure and either a Salac Berry or a Custap Berry, Kleavor is able to deliver a Fighting-type nuke to deal massive damage to any Pokemon that does not resist Fighting. This can be used to weaken a defensive Pokemon or eliminate a fast-but-frail threat such as Meowscarada, Darkrai, or Terrakion.

Endure: Endure allows Kleavor to survive a hit, which is useful for surviving one-time-use priority moves such as First Impression and Fake Out as well as activating pinch berries such as Salac Berry and Custap Berry. Endure also synergizes well with the aforementioned Reversal.

Light Screen: Light Screen can be useful to allow Kleavor to support its teammates by weakening powerful special attackers such as Chi-Yu, Raging Bolt, and Enamorus.

Quick Attack: Quick Attack allows Kleavor to finish off weakened foes, which is especially useful against Pokemon with Sturdy and Pokemon expected to hold a Focus Sash.

Common Items

Choice Scarf: Choice Scarf allows Kleavor to boost its subpar Speed to nearly guarantee it a chance to set Stealth Rock with Stone Axe and provide more offensive value throughout the game.

Heavy-Duty Boots: As Kleavor is vulnerable to Stealth Rock and other entry hazards, it appreciates the immunity to them, especially considering the synergy between Heavy-Duty Boots and U-turn, allowing Kleavor to more effectively be a defensive pivot.

Focus Sash: As Kleavor is relatively frail, Focus Sash is incredibly helpful in allowing it to survive almost any hit and ensure that Stealth Rock gets up through Stone Axe.

Niche Items

Resistance Berries: Resistance Berries are a way to circumvent Kleavor's frailty by letting it survive an attack and set up Stealth Rock with Stone Axe. Resistance Berries also allow Kleavor to lure Rock- and Steel-type Pokemon in and nail them with a super effective Close Combat.

Choice Band: Though Kleavor has a middling Speed stat, when facing teams with slower, bulkier Pokemon, Choice Band is extremely helpful in allowing it to deal more damage and weaken defensive backbones for its teammates.

Salac Berry / Custap Berry: Both Salac and Custap Berry allow Kleavor to outspeed its foes when it reaches low health, which enables its ability to pick off frailer threats, whether it be with one of its Sharpness-boosted STAB moves or Reversal.

Tera

Kleavor receives very little benefit from Terastallizing, so it is not recommended to chose it as a Tera Captain. If you do make it a Tera Captain, however, Terastallizing it into Tera Rock or Bug to further empower its Sharpness-boosted STAB moves is recommended, though it can also Terastallize into Tera Fighting to boost Close Combat. On the other hand, Kleavor can choose to Terastallize into Tera Ghost, giving it a valuable immunity to Rapid Spin.

Draft Strategy

Kleavor should never be the focal point of a draft; instead, it should be picked to complement previous picks through its ability to nearly guarantee setting Stealth Rock. Teams looking for a Stealth Rock user and a pivot can look to Kleavor as an option.

Wallbreakers: Many wallbreakers appreciate Kleavor's ability to get Stealth Rock up, as it allows them to reach certain KO benchmarks that were previously unattainable. This is especially true with special attackers that appreciate Kleavor’s ability to break special walls. Examples include Darkrai, Sneasler, and Chi-Yu.

Entry Hazard Removal Blockers: Since most of Kleavor's value stems from its undeniable Stealth Rock, Ghost-type Pokemon that can block Rapid Spin, such as Gholdengo, Skeledirge, and Pecharunt, are key. In addition, Pokemon that can deny Defog with a fast Taunt, such as Tornadus-T, and Pokemon that deter Defog with Defiant and Competitive, such as Galarian Zapdos and Kilowattrel, make excellent partners.

Fire-, Fighting-, and Ground-type Pokemon: Kleavor's STAB move combination leaves it walled by Steel-type Pokemon, making Pokemon that can break them, such as Sneasler, Garchomp, and Chi-Yu, valuable teammates.

Entry Hazard Control: Due to its frailty and crippling Stealth Rock weakness, Kleavor appreciates spinners such as Great Tusk and Terapagos. While Defoggers such as Corviknight are considerable options, Rapid Spin is slightly preferred, as it allows entry hazards to remain on the opposing side, which is key to Kleavor's main use in getting up Stealth Rock.

Checks and Counters

Steel-type Pokemon: Kleavor's STAB move combination is walled by Steel-types. In particular, Steel-types not weak to its Close Combat are incredible checks, with prime examples being Gholdengo, Tinkaton, and Revavroom. In addition, Iron Crown is an incredible counter to Kleavor, as Tachyon Cutter knocks it out through either Focus Sash or Babiri Berry.

Physically Defensive Pokemon: Kleavor is realistically a one-dimensional physical attacker, thus making physical walls such as Dondozo, Alomomola, and Pecharunt excellent checks.

Contact Effects: If Kleavor is KOed due to contact damage while using Stone Axe, Stealth Rock will not be set. Pokemon like Garchomp and any Pokemon holding a Rocky Helmet can deny Stealth Rock from being set up. Flame Body and Static can also strongly cripple Kleavor.

Faster Threats / Speed-boosting Pokemon: Due to its frail nature, Kleavor is extremely threatened by faster Pokemon. Even with a Choice Scarf, its mediocre Speed leads to it being outsped by common Speed-boosting Pokemon and Choice Scarf users such as Terrakion, Iron Valiant, and Jirachi.

movesets.name: Choice Scarf (Bug)
movesets.description: Choice Scarf Kleavor is one of the best answers to Flying- and Fire-types, like Tornadus-T, Mega Charizard-Y, and Skeledirge, for Bug teams, thanks to its Sharpness-boosted Stone Axe, which has the added utility of automatically setting Stealth Rock. Close Combat synergizes well with Kleavor's STAB moves, crushing Steel-types like Iron Treads. U-turn allows Kleavor to pivot out of Great Tusk and Skarmory to bring in teammates like Araquanid or Volcarona. Night Slash banishes Ghost-types like Gholdengo, Knock Off softens walls like Corviknight and Porygon2 for its teammates, and X-Scissor takes down Slowbro to make way for Mega Pinsir. Araquanid and Galvantula are excellent teammates, as these set up Sticky Web to patch up Kleavor's unassuming speed, even when using a Choice Scarf, allowing it to outspeed Choice Scarf Blacephalon. Additionally, they also help in dealing with pesky Fire- and Flying-types like Volcarona and Landorus, respectively. Physical setup sweepers benefit from Kleavor's ability to set hazards offensively, Knock Off items from walls, and deal with Skeledirge and Slowbro, which often wall Mega Pinsir, Scizor, and Mega Scizor. In return, they deal with Fighting- and Fairy-types like Great Tusk and Mega Diancie. Quiver Dance Volcarona appreciates Skeledirge removed, as this lets it clean up Ghost teams at +1; it can also be brought in against passive walls like Slowbro and Skarmory. Forretress provides Rapid Spin and loves Kleavor's ability to set Stealth Rock, as this allows it to run other hazards like Toxic Spikes or Volt Switch to better support the team. Lokix provides great offensive support with its access to priority in First Impression and Sucker Punch to finish off teams weakened by Kleavor through entry hazards and repeated Knock Offs. It is also a secondary check to Skeledirge, which Bug teams appreciate.
